EXTEND C0001 | FIND: the same availability bug also affects `HealthScan.tools_available` completeness, not just correctness. In `scan_health()`, keys are only populated for the four attempted runners and only inside the try-path. FOLLOW: downstream consumers cannot distinguish "tool absent" from "tool never tracked", and advertised tools (`crosshair`, declared in module constants/docstring) never appear in availability output at all. This corrupts whole-body health reporting and can mislead the insect brain/human reviewer about monitoring coverage. FIX: initialize `tools_available` explicitly for every supported tool and set availability from execution status rather than "runner returned without raising".

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.56
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox imports/dependencies correctly. It copies only the target file into a temp directory (`patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`) and then runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that isolated file. For modules like `bench/endocrine.py` that import `bench.dm._types`, the patched file in tmpdir no longer sits inside the project/package layout, so pyright at minimum evaluates it in a materially different environment than the real source tree. Evidence: the patched file is detached from its original package path; no project tree, sibling modules, or config files are copied; the post-fix analysis runs against `patched_path`, not the original relative location under a sandboxed repo copy.
FOLLOW: This directly breaks function 3’s advertised purpose: fix evaluation can label a safe fix HARMFUL/UNEVALUABLE because imports fail only in the sandbox, or miss breakage caused by interactions with neighboring files/config because those dependencies are absent. That feeds wrong `verified` decisions into the immune pipeline’s Stage 4 in `immune_agents.py`, which in turn drives the bug-closed gate and can silently reject or fail to close real findings.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — sandbox the file within a copied project subtree, not as a lone basename file: create a temp repo copy containing the relevant package/root, write the patch back to the same relative path inside that copy, and run pyright/ruff/bandit/tests from the sandbox root.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` can execute tests against the unmodified source tree instead of the sandboxed patch. It runs `_run_tool(test_cmd, cwd=tmpdir)`, but `test_cmd` is passed through unchanged. In real use from `immune_agents.py`, the command is `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`. Because tmpdir contains only the patched file, not the repo, that relative test path does not refer to the sandboxed codebase; Python/pytest resolution will either fail or import the original project from elsewhere on `sys.path`. Evidence: no rewrite of test paths, no env isolation (`PYTHONPATH` unchanged), and no repo copy exists under tmpdir.
FOLLOW: The core safety claim "sandbox-test proposed fixes (SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL)" becomes unsound. A harmful patch can be marked SAFE because tests ran against the original source, and a safe patch can be marked HARMFUL/UNEVALUABLE because the sandbox lacks the test tree. This propagates into false `verified=True` in the immune pipeline, which can prematurely close bugs and suppress further review.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — run tests only inside a sandboxed repo copy and rewrite/require `test_cmd` to target paths within that copied tree; set `PYTHONPATH`/cwd so imports resolve exclusively to the sandbox.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.48
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` collapses all tool deltas into a single signed sum: `total_net = net_type + net_ruff + net_bandit`, then treats `total_net <= 0` as non-harmful. This lets a fix that introduces a new security or type error still be marked SAFE if it removes more issues elsewhere. Example from the code path: `+1 bandit, -2 ruff, 0 pyright` yields `total_net = -1` → SAFE, despite introducing a new security issue. That contradicts the function docstring: “HARMFUL: new issues introduced”.
FOLLOW: Downstream, the immune pipeline uses SAFE/NEUTRAL to mark findings as `verified`. Under current logic, regressions can be certified as verified fixes, activating the bug-closed gate and preventing further reports on a still-broken or now-worse code path. This is a silently wrong result, so HIGH in PoC terms.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — classify as HARMFUL if any individual net field is positive; classify as SAFE only when at least one field improves and none worsen; otherwise keep existing no-change handling.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.39
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` uses substring matching (`if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`) over paths extracted from free text in `finding.description + " " + finding.proposed_fix`. This can select the wrong file whenever one source path is a substring of another or when the description mentions multiple files. Evidence: the matcher does not prefer exact/basename/unique relative-path resolution and returns the first partial match.
FOLLOW: `evaluate_fix()` may patch and score the wrong file, producing false UNEVALUABLE, false SAFE, or false HARMFUL verdicts. Because fix evaluation is used programmatically by the immune pipeline to mark verified fixes, wrong-file targeting can close the wrong bug while leaving the intended defect untouched.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — resolve file references by exact normalized path match first, then unique basename/unique suffix match; if resolution is ambiguous, return UNEVALUABLE instead of picking the first substring hit.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.68
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.34
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the advertised “health scan — static analysis (pyright/ruff/bandit) between rounds” never reports explicit tool failure diagnostics. When a tool times out, is missing, or emits unparsable output, runners mostly return `[]` and `scan_health()` just aggregates zero diagnostics. Apart from logging, the returned `HealthScan` has no field for execution failure/parse failure counts, so a broken scanner can look identical to a clean codebase.
FOLLOW: This degrades the endocrine layer’s primary role as a health monitor: the insect brain and human reviewer receive “0 diagnostics” without machine-readable evidence that the scan itself failed. Combined with the known availability bug, this can make the monitoring layer fail open and hide that no meaningful scan occurred.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — add minimal machine-readable scan failure reporting to `HealthScan` (e.g. per-tool status/error string) and populate it from each runner on NOT_FOUND/TIMEOUT/parse failure instead of silently returning empty diagnostics.
VERIFIED: TRUE
